compiled_state.description:
## Observation
`make venv` fails on this macOS/arm64 host for any NEW worktree:

```
ERROR: selected uv is version 0.13.6, but this repository requires 0.12.7.
       selected uv: /Users/joeoakhart/.local/share/uv-pins/0.12.7/uv
       required by: pyproject.toml [tool.uv].required-version
```

The error names the contradiction exactly: the binary living at the path `…/uv-pins/**0.12.7**/uv` reported `uv 0.13.6 (329bf9448 2026-10-26 aarch64-apple-darwin)`. The pin directory is a version-named path, and the binary inside it had been replaced in place with a NEWER build — dated the same day the failure appeared, and with the directory mtime inside the active session window.

`uvx` in the same directory was untouched and still reported `0.12.7 (61291a8ca 2026-08-27)`. So exactly one of the two binaries was swapped, which is the signature of an in-place self-update of `uv` alone (`uv self update` rewrites the running binary at its own path) rather than of a re-provisioned pin directory.

## Impact
This breaks worktree creation, which is the documented entry point for ALL work in this repo (`make worktree name=<branch>`, and the `make venv` + `make install` bootstrap in `docs/local-dev-env.md`). It fails closed and the message is accurate, so it is not silent — but it is also not self-describing: the path says `0.12.7` while the binary says `0.13.6`, which reads as a repo misconfiguration rather than a mutated host file.

Existing worktrees are unaffected — their `.venv` directories already exist, so nothing re-resolves `uv`. The failure therefore appears only when a new worktree is provisioned, which is precisely when an agent is starting new work.

A version-named directory whose contents can be silently rewritten is not a pin. It is a naming convention with no enforcement.

## Verified workaround (applied on this host, not committed)
Restore the matching release binary at the pinned path:

```sh
cd ~/.local/share/uv-pins/0.12.7
cp uv uv.0.13.6.bak
curl -sL -o /tmp/uv.tgz \
  https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/0.12.7/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
tar xzf /tmp/uv.tgz -C /tmp && cp /tmp/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin/uv ./uv && chmod +x ./uv
```

`uv --version` then reports `0.12.7 (61291a8ca 2026-08-27)` and `make venv` succeeds (`Using CPython 3.12.14`, venv created). The displaced 0.13.6 binary is kept alongside as `uv.0.13.6.bak`.

## Proposed fix (needs a decision)
The workaround repairs one host. Options for preventing recurrence, in rough order of preference:

1. **Verify the pin, not just its path.** Have the `make venv` preflight compare `uv --version` against `[tool.uv] required-version` BEFORE selecting the binary, and on mismatch fetch the required release into the pin directory automatically. Self-healing, portable, no CI-provider coupling.
2. **Make the pin directory immutable** (read-only mode bits on the binary), so an in-place self-update fails loudly at the moment it happens rather than at the next worktree creation.
3. **Content-address the pin** — name the directory by the release's checksum, so a replaced binary no longer resolves and the mismatch cannot masquerade as the pinned version.
4. **Document only**, in `docs/local-dev-env.md`: record the failure signature and the restore recipe. Cheapest, but leaves the next agent to rediscover it.

Option 1 is recommended but NOT yet decided: it needs confirmation that fetching a release binary during bootstrap is acceptable in this project's supply-chain posture (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, and the dependency-update rules in `CONTRIBUTING.md` §5).

Unverified: what actually ran the update. No shell history or installer log was inspected, so `uv self update` is inferred from the single-binary swap and the in-place rewrite, not observed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a host whose pin directory holds a mismatched binary, `make venv` either repairs the pin or fails with a message that names the mutation ("the binary at <pinned path> reports <X>, not the <Y> its path claims") rather than only the version mismatch.
- [ ] A newly provisioned worktree (`make worktree name=<x>`) completes `make venv` and `make install` with no manual intervention on such a host.
- [ ] The chosen mechanism introduces no CI-provider-specific trigger: it runs from the documented local bootstrap, not only from a GitHub Actions step.
- [ ] `docs/local-dev-env.md` records the failure signature and the operator restore recipe.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
compiled_state.title: make venv fails for new worktrees: the uv binary inside the 0.12.7 pin directory was replaced with 0.13.6
